subject: VALUE clause
notes: kb/Work PB556, LANDED. "Formats 3 and 5 may be specified only when the level-number of the subject of the entry is 88" (cite --check OK, §13.18.63.3 33)) is now screened at bind time, COBOL2167, over a SET of the format-3/5-only phrases rather than three hand-written conditions: the THROUGH phrase and the IN alphabet-name phrase (formats 3 and 5), WHEN SET TO FALSE (format 3), VALID / INVALID (format 5). The grammar admits every VALUE format through ONE rule on purpose — formats 3 and 5 share their literal / THROUGH list — so the format-vs-level rule is the binder's, and the set is what makes a phrase added to that rule tomorrow screened by adding one line. MEASURED BEFORE and AFTER on this worktree's own build: `01 X PIC 9 VALUE 1 THRU 5.` failed the whole Roslyn compilation (CS1002 + two CS1519s, no COBOL diagnostic) and now reports COBOL2167; `05 X PIC XXX VALUE "A" THRU "C".` compiled CLEAN and stored the glued source text `"A` and now reports COBOL2167; `01 X PIC 9 VALUE 1 WHEN SET TO FALSE IS 0.` was accepted and the phrase dropped in silence; `01 X PIC XX VALUE "AA" IN AL1.` likewise. Level 77 behaves as level 01 (v33d's shape). The level-88 population is unchanged — conformance:wiseowl/cases/13.18.63-VALUE/pb556_condition_formats_stay_legal_at_88 is the over-reject guard the three negatives cannot be. The VALID / INVALID arm is in the set but unobservable today: DeclinedFacilityPass refuses every A.4.14 content-validation surface by name (COBOL1708) in a pass that runs before the binder, at any level.
